points.title: 早年求学
points.description: 阿基米德出生于西西里岛的叙拉古（今意大利锡拉库萨），是一位天文学家之子。早年，他可能曾在亚历山大港学习，那里是当时世界的学术中心。在这段时期，他接触到了欧几里得的数学著作，并开始研究数学和物理学的基础理论。他发明了一种螺旋泵（阿基米德螺旋），至今仍在使用。这段学习经历为他后来的科学成就奠定了坚实基础，培养了他对数学和物理学的浓厚兴趣。
points.descriptionEn: Archimedes was born in Syracuse, a Greek city-state in Sicily (now Italy), to an astronomer father. In his early years, he likely studied in Alexandria, then the world's intellectual center, where he encountered the works of Euclid and began his foundational studies in mathematics and physics. During this period, he invented the Archimedean screw, a device still in use today. This educational experience laid the groundwork for his later scientific achievements and fostered his deep interest in mathematics and physics.

points.title: 数学研究
points.description: 在亚历山大港期间，阿基米德与当时最杰出的学者交流，包括埃拉托色尼和科农。他发展了穷竭法，这是一种早期的积分学方法，用于计算面积和体积。他计算出了圆周率的近似值，并证明了球体体积与其外接圆柱体体积的关系。他还研究了杠杆原理和浮力定律，这些发现后来成为他最著名的成就之一。在亚历山大港的学术氛围中，阿基米德迅速成长为一位杰出的数学家和物理学家，为他的科学事业奠定了坚实基础。
points.descriptionEn: During his time in Alexandria, Archimedes interacted with leading scholars including Eratosthenes and Conon. He developed the method of exhaustion, an early form of integral calculus for calculating areas and volumes. He approximated the value of pi and proved the relationship between the volume of a sphere and its circumscribed cylinder. He also studied the principles of levers and buoyancy, which later became among his most famous achievements. In Alexandria's intellectual environment, Archimedes rapidly developed into a distinguished mathematician and physicist, laying a solid foundation for his scientific career.

points.title: 科学应用
points.description: 返回叙拉古后，阿基米德将他的科学知识应用于解决实际问题。他设计了许多机械装置，包括复合滑轮系统、投石机和起重机械。最著名的是他利用杠杆原理设计的机械系统，据称能移动重物。他还发明了阿基米德燃烧镜，一种能聚焦阳光点燃敌船的装置。在国王希伦二世的委托下，阿基米德解决了王冠纯度问题，发现了浮力原理，即著名的'阿基米德原理'。这一时期，他将理论与实践紧密结合，展示了科学知识的实用价值。
points.descriptionEn: Returning to Syracuse, Archimedes applied his scientific knowledge to solve practical problems. He designed numerous mechanical devices including compound pulley systems, catapults, and lifting machines. Most famously, he designed mechanical systems based on the lever principle, reportedly capable of moving heavy objects. He also invented the Archimedes death ray, a device that could focus sunlight to set enemy ships on fire. At King Hiero II's request, Archimedes solved the problem of determining the purity of a crown, discovering the principle of buoyancy, now known as Archimedes' principle. During this period, he closely integrated theory with practice, demonstrating the practical value of scientific knowledge.

points.title: 保卫叙拉古
points.description: 当罗马军队开始入侵西西里岛时，阿基米德利用他的科学知识帮助保卫叙拉古。他设计了各种防御机械，包括巨型起重机，能吊起罗马船只并摧毁它们；他改进的投石机能将巨石射向敌军；据传他还使用了'阿基米德燃烧镜'点燃罗马舰队。阿基米德的防御措施极为有效，罗马军队在围城两年多后才攻陷城市。尽管年事已高，阿基米德仍然积极参与城市的防御工作，展现了科学家在危机时刻的勇气和责任感。
points.descriptionEn: As Roman armies began to invade Sicily, Archimedes used his scientific knowledge to help defend Syracuse. He designed various defensive mechanisms including giant cranes that could lift Roman ships and destroy them; improved catapults that hurled boulders at enemy troops; and reportedly used the 'Archimedes death ray' to set the Roman fleet on fire. Archimedes' defensive measures were highly effective, and the Romans took over two years to capture the city despite the siege. Despite his advanced age, Archimedes actively participated in the city's defense, demonstrating the courage and sense of responsibility of a scientist in times of crisis.

points.title: 逝世与遗产
points.description: 公元前212年，罗马军队攻陷叙拉古。据传，当一名罗马士兵进入阿基米德的住所时，他正在沙地上研究数学问题，并喊道'不要打扰我的圆圈'。尽管罗马将军马塞勒斯曾下令不得伤害阿基米德，但他仍被杀害。阿基米德的死被视为科学史上的一大悲剧。他的著作被保存下来，对后来的科学发展产生了深远影响，包括伽利略、牛顿等科学巨匠都曾研究他的工作。阿基米德被视为古代最伟大的科学家之一，他的数学方法、物理原理和工程应用为后世科学发展奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 212 BC, Roman forces captured Syracuse. According to tradition, when a Roman soldier entered Archimedes' home, he was studying mathematical problems drawn in the sand and exclaimed, 'Do not disturb my circles.' Despite orders from General Marcellus to spare Archimedes, he was killed. Archimedes' death is considered a great tragedy in the history of science. His works were preserved and had a profound impact on later scientific development, including studies by giants like Galileo and Newton. Archimedes is regarded as one of the greatest scientists of antiquity, and his mathematical methods, physical principles, and engineering applications laid the foundation for future scientific progress.

supporter.zh: 阿基米德被视为古代最伟大的科学家之一，他的贡献跨越数学、物理学和工程学领域。他开创性的数学方法为后世微积分的发展奠定了基础，而他的物理原理至今仍在应用。阿基米德展现了理论与实践的完美结合，将抽象的数学概念转化为解决实际问题的工具。他的科学精神和求知态度激励了无数后来的科学家，是人类理性思维的典范。
supporter.en: Archimedes is regarded as one of the greatest scientists of antiquity, whose contributions spanned mathematics, physics, and engineering. His innovative mathematical methods laid the foundation for the later development of calculus, and his physical principles remain in use today. Archimedes demonstrated the perfect integration of theory and practice, transforming abstract mathematical concepts into tools for solving practical problems. His scientific spirit and quest for knowledge have inspired countless later scientists, making him a paragon of human rational thought.

critic.zh: 批评者指出阿基米德的工作过于注重理论而缺乏系统性，他的许多发现未能得到广泛应用或发展。此外，他对实际问题的解决方案有时过于复杂，缺乏实用性。阿基米德对数学的执着也使他忽视了其他科学领域的发展。他的著作在古代传播有限，直到中世纪晚期才被重新发现，这限制了其影响力的及时发挥。批评者认为，如果他能更好地记录和传播他的发现，科学发展的进程可能会加速。
critic.en: Critics point out that Archimedes' work was overly focused on theory without systematic development, and many of his discoveries failed to see widespread application or further development. Additionally, his solutions to practical problems were sometimes overly complex and lacked practicality. Archimedes' obsession with mathematics also caused him to neglect developments in other scientific fields. His works had limited circulation in antiquity and were not rediscovered until the late Middle Ages, which limited the timely impact of his influence. Critics argue that if he had better documented and disseminated his findings, the progress of science might have accelerated.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，阿基米德被符号化为'古代最伟大的科学家'，代表着人类理性思维的巅峰。他的生平故事，包括'尤里卡'时刻和'不要打扰我的圆圈'的临终遗言，已成为科学探索精神的象征。阿基米德的工作连接了古代希腊的数学传统与后来的科学革命，他的方法预示了现代科学的发展方向。在流行文化中，他常被描绘为天才发明家，形象既崇高又人性化，体现了科学探索的激情与执着。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Archimedes has been symbolized as 'the greatest scientist of antiquity,' representing the pinnacle of human rational thought. His life stories, including the 'Eureka' moment and his dying words 'Do not disturb my circles,' have become symbols of the scientific spirit. Archimedes' work connected the mathematical traditions of ancient Greece with later scientific revolutions, and his methods anticipated the direction of modern scientific development. In popular culture, he is often depicted as a genius inventor, both sublime and human, embodying the passion and dedication of scientific exploration.

self.zh: 给我一个支点，我就能撬动整个地球。
self.en: Give me a place to stand, and I shall move the Earth.

others.zh: 阿基米德是古代最伟大的数学家，他的智慧超越了时代，为后世科学发展奠定了基础。
others.en: Archimedes was the greatest mathematician of antiquity, whose wisdom transcended his time and laid the foundation for future scientific development.
